Pooled result

Estimate withdrawn. WITHDRAWN 2026-08-18. The four trials do not measure the same thing, and one of them does not measure an event at all. Registered primaries read from ClinicalTrials.gov on 2026-08-18: FIDELIO-DKD (NCT02540993) a KIDNEY-FAILURE composite; FIGARO-DKD (NCT02545049) a composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke and heart-failure hospitalisation; FINEARTS-HF (NCT04435626) cardiovascular death and total heart-failure events; ARTS-DN (NCT01874431) 'ratio of uacr at day 90 to uacr at baseline'. Three different event composites and a continuous albuminuria ratio were pooled as a single odds ratio. ARTS-DN's 0.385 is not an odds ratio; it is a ratio of a continuous biomarker, and it entered a pool of event risks. No harmonised outcome exists at any rank -- checked before withdrawing, per the SGLT2 lesson -- because ARTS-DN is a phase 2b biomarker trial with no cardiovascular outcome data. There is no replacement pool and that is the honest position.

Multiple trial-declared outcomes: The First Occurrence of the Composite Endpoint of Onset of Kidney Failure, a Sustained Decrease of eGFR ≥40% From Baseli | The First Occurrence of the Composite Endpoint of Cardiovascular Death, Non-fatal Myocardial Infarction, Non Fatal Strok | Occurrence of the Composite Endpoint of Cardiovascular Death and Total (First and Recurrent) Heart Failure Events | Ratio of uacr at Day 90 to uacr at Baseline. k = 3.

What this does not establishNot that finerenone is ineffective, and not that any of these trials is poor -- each reports its own registered primary correctly. Introduction

Background. This review asks: In adults with heart failure, does Finerenone (BAY94-8862) compared with placebo affect the outcome each trial registered as its primary, which differ across the 3 trials here? It examines 3 randomised trials and does not pool them. The outcome sought is Multiple trial-declared outcomes: The First Occurrence of the Composite Endpoint of Onset of Kidney Failure, a Sustained Decrease of eGFR ≥40% From Baseli | The First Occurrence of the Composite Endpoint of Cardiovascular Death, Non-fatal Myocardial Infarction, Non Fatal Strok | Occurrence of the Composite Endpoint of Cardiovascular Death and Total (First and Recurrent) Heart Failure Events | Ratio of uacr at Day 90 to uacr at Baseline.1

Results

Multiple trial-declared outcomes: The First Occurrence of the Composite Endpoint of Onset of Kidney Failure, a Sustained Decrease of eGFR ≥40% From Baseli | The First Occurrence of the Composite Endpoint of Cardiovascular Death, Non-fatal Myocardial Infarction, Non Fatal Strok | Occurrence of the Composite Endpoint of Cardiovascular Death and Total (First and Recurrent) Heart Failure Events | Ratio of uacr at Day 90 to uacr at Baseline. These 3 trials are not pooled, and the reason is stated rather than the outcome being quietly omitted: Withdrawn 2026-08-18. The four trials do not measure the same thing, and one of them does not measure an event at all. Registered primaries read from ClinicalTrials.gov on 2026-08-18: FIDELIO-DKD (NCT02540993) a KIDNEY-FAILURE composite; FIGARO-DKD (NCT02545049) a composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke and heart-failure hospitalisation; FINEARTS-HF (NCT04435626) cardiovascular death and total heart-failure events; ARTS-DN (NCT01874431) 'ratio of uacr at day 90 to uacr at baseline'. Three different event composites and a continuous albuminuria ratio were pooled as a single odds ratio. ARTS-DN's 0.385 is not an odds ratio; it is a ratio of a continuous biomarker, and it entered a pool of event risks. No harmonised outcome exists at any rank -- checked before withdrawing, per the SGLT2 lesson -- because ARTS-DN is a phase 2b biomarker trial with no cardiovascular outcome data. There is no replacement pool and that is the honest position.1

Limitations

What this review does not give a clinician: the number of events in each arm, any absolute effect or number needed to treat and any measure of harm. A relative effect cannot be turned into the benefit or the risk facing one patient without them, so this review can support a judgement about what these trials found and not a judgement about what to do.1
